rule: A CrossConcept must be an additional concept outside the primary L3/L4 decisive method. CC_DISCRIMINANT duplicates a discriminant-primary item; CC_INEQUALITY_QUADRATIC names the target/primary quadratic inequality rather than an independent extra method in these five items.

items.reason: The upward quadratic is nonnegative for all real x exactly when D≤0. That discriminant test is the primary method itself; no second canonical concept enters the decisive step.
Existence of negative values is converted to D>0 after a sign change. The sign condition and discriminant calculation form the single primary quadratic test, not a separate CrossConcept.
The two requested root/sign cases use D=0 and D≤0 on the same quadratic. Their distinction is a parameter condition within the primary discriminant method.

A positive quadratic inequality with no solutions is rewritten as global nonpositivity and checked by leading coefficient plus D. Both checks belong to the primary quadratic-discriminant classification; its separate IntegrationPattern remains under Sol review.
Each statement is classified by a repeated-root discriminant and strict-versus-inclusive endpoint. Endpoint rigor is a condition of the same primary test, not an additional CrossConcept.
